title: Minimum Partition Score
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, partition nums into exactly k subarrays.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, partition nums into exactly k subarrays. The goal is to find the minimum possible score among all valid partitions. The score of a subarray is defined as the sum of its elements, sumArr, multiplied by (sumArr + 1) / 2.
constraints: nums has up to 1,000 positive values and 1≤k≤n.
Partition into exactly k nonempty contiguous subarrays.
A segment of sum s costs s(s+1)/2; minimize total cost.
hints: Expand f(Pi-Pj) so each previous cut j contributes a line of slope -Pj queried at x=Pi.
Positive nums make prefix sums and query x values strictly increasing, while new line slopes strictly decrease.
Maintain the lower hull in a deque for each group count and query it monotonically.
The algebra equals the exact segment cost, and the DP considers every last cut while hull dominance removes only lines that can never be optimal.
editorial: The algebra equals the exact segment cost, and the DP considers every last cut while hull dominance removes only lines that can never be optimal.

tests.explanation: Splitting as [5] and [1,2,1] costs fifteen plus ten, totaling twenty-five.
Three singleton segments each cost one, totaling three.
